discovery: Prediction and experimental realization of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects

nominees.name: Qi-Kun Xue
nominees.affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech), Shenzhen, and Tsinghua University, China

subfield: Condensed matter physics / topological quantum materials
motivation: Topological insulators established a new classification of electronic matter, in which band topology, not symmetry breaking, protects conducting edge and surface states. Kane (with Mele) predicted the quantum spin Hall state and developed the Z2 topological invariant theory that defines the field. Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental proof, observing quantized edge conduction in HgTe quantum wells in 2007 after a remarkable feat of heterostructure growth. Xue's team used exceptionally precise molecular beam epitaxy of magnetically doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 films to observe the quantum anomalous Hall effect in 2013: a quantized Hall resistance with no external magnetic field, a result many thought beyond experimental reach. Together the three achievements show that theory and atomic-scale control of crystal growth can create new quantum states of matter. They have shaped a large international field, from Majorana platforms to dissipationless electronics and metrology.
